title: Brandenburg Gate
blurb: Carl Gotthard Langhans’ neoclassical city gate in Berlin, built 1788 to 1791. Twelve 15 m Doric columns in two rows form five passageways, and a copper Quadriga of Victoria driving a four-horse chariot crowns the attic.

sourceUrls.label: ad-hoc-news.de: Brandenburger Tor and the Quadriga

systems.name: Doric colonnades
systems.description: Twelve 15 m fluted Doric columns in a front and a rear row, with echinus-and-abacus capitals and no bases, in the Greek manner.

systems.name: Passageway walls and Hercules reliefs
systems.description: The six walls between the front and rear column pairs, dividing the five passageways, with classicizing reliefs of the Labors of Hercules.

systems.name: Entablature
systems.description: Architrave, triglyph frieze with sixteen metopes on each long face, and cornice.

systems.name: Attic storey
systems.description: The plain attic with the Triumph of Peace relief, side steps, and the second cornice carrying the Quadriga.

systems.name: Quadriga
systems.description: Schadow’s copper four-horse chariot, about 5 m high, driven by Victoria and facing east into the city.

systems.name: Side wings
systems.description: L-shaped flanking wings at lower height in the same Doric order, with open stoas, custom houses, angled roofs, pediments and statues.

systems.name: Passageway floors
systems.description: The floors of the five passageways between the transverse walls.

systems.name: Steps and platform
systems.description: Front and rear steps and the column platform the gate stands on.
